ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) 'List of Terrorist Entities', Global Affairs Canada sanctions registers maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, and domestic FINTRAC suspicious transaction guidance. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where PEP status is detected, with source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal for official corporate name clearance and reservation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate legal form must be expressed in French, e.g., 'Société par actions', 'Compagnie', or accepted abbreviations; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, requires that the distinguishing element of the name be in French, with limited exceptions for recognized foreign expressions, marks, and personal names. Non-Latin scripts require transliteration into Latin characters and French phonetic compatibility.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Obscene, scandalous, or inciting hatred terms
Placement, Fonds de placement (if not licensed)
Words suggesting a Crown, municipal, or public-agency connection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is refused, the applicant may request a written statement of reasons from the Registraire. Within 30 days of the refusal, the applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the Registraire under section 126 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-45. If the reconsideration is rejected, the applicant may institute a judicial-review application before the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of that decision, preserving a prior name-reservation alternative for re-submission through the REQ portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the exclusive registered-office function only if the service provider maintains a physical street address in Quebec, accepts service of legal and government documents during business hours, and is not a mere post-office box or non-serviceable virtual mailbox. Virtual offices are not a substitute for commercial substance where tax-treaty or Revenu Québec GST/QST registration requirements demand physical or personnel presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% annual likelihood for a low-risk LegalTech SaaS corporation with standard payment rails, no high-risk activity, and no statutory licensing requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Québec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, Chapter II (Incorporation), Chapter III (Organization and powers of the corporation), Chapter IV (Directors and officers), and Chapter XXI (Records and returns); Regulation respecting the Registraire des entreprises, CQLR c E-8.1, r 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) acting through the Registraire central des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts de constitution) filed through the Registraire central des entreprises / Entreprises Québec online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; the corporation may issue shares with or without par value and no escrow deposit or advance capital pledge is required. Shares are non-assessable when consideration fixed and payable to the corporation in respect of their issue has been received or is receivable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Corporation by articles filed with the Québec Enterprise Registrar and the Certificate of Incorporation are ratified; that the common shares set forth in the share subscription schedule are allotted and issued for the stated consideration; that the registered office is established at [address in Québec]; that [director names] are appointed directors; that [officer names] are elected Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary; and that those officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete filings to implement the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Quebec Name Compliance Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Entreprises Québec online services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search in the Registraire central des entreprises for identical or confusingly similar names, verify legality and compliance with the Charter of the French Language, and file a name reservation request with a primary name and alternative names.
required_dossiers: Written consent if the name contains a personal name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, incorporate under an approved alternative name or file a reconsideration request with additional distinguishing words; a reserved name may be renewed by filing a further reservation request and fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Registraire central des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes the articles of incorporation based on the model form, specifying the corporate name, authorized share structure, restrictions, number of directors, and initial registered office. Submit the articles online together with the declaration of registration and pay the prescribed filing fee.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate or proof of approved name
Consent to act as director (if not included in articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query, respond within the prescribed period by correcting inconsistencies, filing a redrafted document, and paying any deficient fee; incomplete articles may be withdrawn and refiled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Admission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completed registration, the Registrar issues the certificate of incorporation and a registry extract. Verify the corporate name, registration number, directors, and registered office shown in the extract, and deposit the certificate in the corporation’s records. The registered office must be a valid address in Québec and must be recorded in the registry.
required_dossiers: Registry extract from the Registraire central des entreprises
Proof of corporate registration and jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or extract contains errors, file a claim for rectification with the Registrar; if the registered office is refused, provide a compliant Québec address and file an updated declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutional Meeting and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal corporate governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution. Approve the general corporate by-law, adopt the first board resolution, establish the registered office, appoint officers, and authorize banking. Record all resolutions in the minutes register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A defective resolution may be cured by calling a further meeting or obtaining a unanimous written resolution that ratifies and corrects the prior record; invalid officer appointments can be ratified by shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Share Subscription and Securities Ledger Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record each subscriber’s subscription agreement, issue share certificates against the authorized share classes, and enter all members in the register of members. Ensure that no share is issued unless the consideration fixed by the directors is received or receivable, and update the capitalization table.
required_dossiers: Cancelled and issued stock certificate stubs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any invalid issuance or overissue should be corrected by cancelling affected certificates and re-issuing them under a fresh board resolution; unpaid consideration may be collected or the allotment reversed under Québec corporate procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Payroll and Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Canadian Business Number, register for GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed the federal threshold, register for QST with Revenu Québec, and open payroll accounts in preparation for hiring. Use the certificate of incorporation and registry extract to complete electronic registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused or delayed, contact CRA or Revenu Québec business number support, confirm the compatible account and file an amendment through the respective secure portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Records, Annual Declaration and Regulatory Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain registers of directors, officers, members, minutes, and accounting records. File the annual declaration with the Registraire central des entreprises within 60 days of the registration anniversary, and report changes of directors or registered office within 15 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late annual declarations may be cured by immediate electronic filing with payment of the prescribed late fee; if the corporation is struck off, apply for revival and pay all arrears and reinstatement fees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541199 LegalTech cloud document automation and e-signature activity does not trigger an industrial manufacturing licence in Quéebec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no provincial industrial operating permit is mandated for non-manufacturing software services conducted from a standard commercial office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity does not appear on the mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment and Review schedule and does not require an authorization as an industrial pollutant source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge thresholds apply to the software activity. Tenancy must comply with the building landlord’s municipal sewer, stormwater, and waste-management obligations, including the Code de gestion des matières résiduelles and municipal by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased commercial office space, the landlord must supply a valid certificate of occupancy or municipal fire safety certificate, the premises must comply with the Québec Building Code and structural load requirements, and the employer must observe CNESST occupational health and safety regulations, fire evacuation planning, and workplace first-aid requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST and corporate income tax administration and business registration portal (Business Registration Online, My Business Account: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec corporate income tax administration (Mon dossier d'entreprise / Clé d'accès: https://www.revenuquebec.ca). The 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) is Canada's statutory TIN; the QST program account is established as the BN suffix 'TQ 0001'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Corporate domestic protocol: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act and obtain the 9-digit NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) from the Registraire d'entreprises du Québec (REQ); no minimum paid-in capital is required. (2) Register with CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN); activate the RT program account for federal corporate tax (T2) and the RC program account for GST/HST. (3) Register the BN with Revenu Québec via Mon dossier d'entreprise to open the TQ (QST) account and the CP account for Quebec corporate income tax; QST registration is mandatory once taxable supplies made in Quebec exceed the CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold plus the worldwide small supplier test. (4) For a foreign-incorporated entity with no Canadian residence, apply for CRA's non-resident GST/HST registration under the simplified cross-border digital services regime, and simultaneously file the corresponding Revenu Québec QST registration for non-resident suppliers of intangible personal property/services; registration is compulsory once the non-resident's worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, even absent a Canadian permanent establishment. (5) Maintain an active annual registration: update the NEQ/BN within 30 days of address/director changes and file the required information returns with the Registraire d'entreprises and Revenu Québec to keep the tax identity enforceable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer from its shareholders under the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act. It pays federal corporate income tax on worldwide income if a Canadian resident; Quebec provincial tax applies to the same taxable income base with provincial adjustments. No pass-through of tax attributes to shareholders occurs; distributions are taxable as eligible/non-eligible dividends. The corporation is not eligible for the small business deduction if it is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), which occurs when 50% or more of the equity is controlled by non-residents; this does not change Entity_Level_Taxation status. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable — no free-zone income exemption exists for cloud/SaaS income in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box-style elective entity reclassification; a corporation is mandatorily an entity-level taxpayer. Available elections relevant to this LegalTech SaaS structure: (1) Closely-related-corporations election under ETA s. 156 and the corresponding QST grouping election — permits intra-group supplies of e-signature/cloud services to be deemed consideration-free, eliminating provincial/federal VAT leakage; (2) functional currency election under ITA s. 261 allowing USD-denominated tax returns if U.S. export revenue is material; (3) ITA s. 93(1) paid-up-capital election on dividends repatriated from a foreign affiliate; (4) ITA s. 216 net-basis election for non-resident recipients of royalty/licence income; (5) Hybrid-mismatch alignment — OECD anti-hybrid rules in ITA ss. 94, 94.2, 94.3 and s. 18(5.1) deny double deductions for hybrid entity/arrangement structures; no elective carve-out exists, and the taxpayer must self-assess under the Canadian hybrid-mismatch ordering rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/QST — dual federal/provincial value-added tax: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) administered by CRA under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) administered by Revenu Québec under the Quebec Taxation Act. Quebec is not an HST harmonized province, so separate registrations, filings, and remittances are required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — annual worldwide taxable supplies threshold for the GST/HST small supplier exemption (ETA s. 148) and the mirrored QST small supplier threshold in Quebec. For cloud document automation and e-signature SaaS, once cumulative worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any calendar quarter or trailing four-quarter period, mandatory registration with CRA and Revenu Québec begins. The same CAD 30,000 worldwide threshold applies to non-resident digital suppliers under the simplified cross-border GST/QST registration regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-clearance API, or digital stamping is imposed on GST/QST invoices; Canada uses a periodic self-assessment model. GST/HST returns (Form GST34-1) and QST returns (Form QST-1) must be transmitted electronically via CRA and Revenu Québec E-file/API channels within one month after the reporting period; no line-item invoice validation occurs at submission. Electronic invoice mandates are limited: (i) Quebec B2G — suppliers invoicing Quebec public bodies must transmit compliant electronic invoices through the provincial electronic invoicing platform integrated with Revenu Québec; (ii) federal Pan-Canadian PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoicing standard — voluntary B2B adoption; (iii) no tax-authority clearance or digital stamping applies to B2B/B2C SaaS invoices. However, the zero-rated export status must be evidenced at the invoice level and documents are demandable by CRA and Revenu Québec on audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply of cloud-based document automation, e-signature authentication, and legal contract SaaS qualifies for 0% GST/QST export zero-rating under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act (supply of intangible personal property) and the mirrored QST provisions, provided: (1) the recipient is a non-resident of Canada for GST/QST purposes; (2) the supply is not made to an individual physically present in Canada at the time of supply; (3) the digital service does not relate to real property situated in Canada and is not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; (4) the service is delivered wholly or substantially through remote electronic access, with no employee or server activity physically performed in Canada for the specific supply; and (5) the supplier retains contemporaneous export substantiation evidencing the non-resident status of the subscriber and the place of use. Pure digital delivery requires no CBSA customs export declaration; the exporter must instead retain transactional and technical logs sufficient to demonstrate the zero-rated character of the supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Non-resident status documentation: statutory declaration or Certificate of Residence for the subscriber/affiliate (e.g., treaty Form NR-303 available to the non-resident recipient) establishing the recipient's tax residence outside Canada

Invoice and contract bundle: fully executed SaaS subscription / EULA / legal contract automation agreement plus commercial invoice marked '0% GST/QST — Export of digital service under ETA Schedule VI Part V and QST mirror provisions' (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541199)

Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103, Stripe settlement ledger, or credit card acquiring receipts demonstrating foreign-currency payment from the non-resident recipient and settlement into the Canadian corporation's bank account

Service delivery audit log: e-signature authentication metadata, server access logs, geo-IP records, and timestamping authority certificates showing user authentication events and service performance occurred outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess an export zero-rating claim within the normal 4-year limitation period, extended to 7 years for negligent misrepresentation, and without limitation where fraud is established. Civil penalties under ETA s. 280/281 impose not less than CAD 5,000 and up to 20% of the tax evaded; Quebec's false-statement penalty under the Tax Administration Act can reach 30% of the QST evaded; prescribed arrears interest is compounded daily and cannot be waived for gross negligence. Upon audit rejection, the invoice is recomputed as a taxable Quebec supply at 14.975% combined GST/QST, input tax credits previously claimed on related inputs are denied, and the resulting tax plus penalties is fully clawed back retroactively. Willful evasion exposes officers/directors to fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment for up to 2 years under ETA s. 282, with Quebec penal provisions authorizing fines up to CAD 50,000 for repeat offenders; a false claim of zero-rated export constitutes tax fraud under Criminal Code s. 380(1) punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day field serves as our internal compliance benchmark — export balances outstanding beyond 180 days trigger a formal documentation refresh and heightened transfer-pricing scrutiny of the intercompany settlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is Canada's sole monetary authority and currency issuer. There is no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration; exchange-control-related regulatory oversight is exercised by the Minister of Finance and operationalized through the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility consistent with IMF Article VIII obligations. No exchange-control approval is required for inbound equity contributions, external borrowing, dividend declarations, or profit repatriation. The principal limitations on remittance are fiscal rather than monetary: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax applies to dividends paid to non-residents at a statutory rate of 25%, generally treaty-reduced to 5-15% under the Canada-U.S. and similar treaties, and transfer pricing or thin capitalization rules may apply. Dividend remittance must be documented through a corporate board resolution and form filed with the Canada Revenue Agency for any treaty-based relief claim.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no statutory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline within which export receipts must be repatriated or converted to Canadian dollars. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency in authorized foreign-currency bank accounts. However, export transactions must be properly documented for corporate income tax, GST/HST purposes, customs valuation, and any applicable Canadian economic sanctions and export-control screening.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary collection rail and Medium-Low as the primary treasury settlement anchor. A foreign electronic-money institution is not recognized as a deposit-taking institution under Canadian banking law, cannot accept regulated deposits, cannot issue commercial letters of credit, and does not carry CDIC deposit insurance. To operate lawfully, a foreign EMI or digital payment provider must register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC, appoint a Canadian designated compliance officer, maintain equivalent Canadian AML/KYC procedures, and require a Canadian Schedule I bank to act as the settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act does not impose a universal statutory requirement for directors to appear physically at a bank branch. A low-risk Quebec Business Corporation may generally complete remote onboarding through secure video KYC interviews, a current Registraire des entreprises du Québec extract, and certified identity documents. In practice, RBC and National Bank will accept remote opening when beneficial ownership is transparent and all directors provide source of funds evidence. A physical appearance at a branch or notarized identity verification will be required if the ownership structure is opaque, a director resides in a high-risk jurisdiction, or the company seeks significant USD credit facilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership or undisclosed significant control person under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and FINTRAC KYC rules
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Registraire des entreprises du Québec registry extract; articles of incorporation and by-laws; official registers of directors and ultimate beneficial owners; shareholder ledger; notarized declaration of no bearer shares and no undisclosed nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious inbound capital injection from a foreign legal-tech parent, venture fund, or crypto-adjacent source
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements of the investing entity; notarized board resolution authorizing the capital contribution; executed share subscription or shareholder loan agreement; source-of-wealth statement; bank reference letter from the remitting bank; clear flow-of-funds diagram and commercial rationale tied to the SaaS legal-contract automation business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency ambiguity or non-resident directors signaling weaker Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number confirmation; advance tax-residency certificate or Form NR73 request; director affidavits detailing physical presence, employment, and personal ties; Quebec Revenu principal-establishment declarations; board minutes showing where strategic decisions are made.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, or exposure to high-risk jurisdictions within the supplier or customer base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated OSFI, DFO, and OFAC sanctions screening results with false-positive analysis; transaction-by-transaction economic justification reports; AML/CFT institutional compliance policy and training evidence; legal opinion on compliance with Canadian economic sanctions and export control laws; customer and supplier due-diligence files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage LegalTech SaaS revenue profile with heavy card-not-present processing, cross-border settlement, and refund or chargeback anomalies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer terms of service and subscription agreements; merchant processing agreements with Stripe and card networks; PCI-DSS attestation of compliance; refund and chargeback policies; enterprise customer KYC files; audit logs of e-signature authentication and contract-execution workflow evidencing legitimate document-automation services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for inbound treasury is: foreign parent bank to an international correspondent, then onward to the Canadian corporate account at National Bank or RBC via SWIFT MT103 for direct payment instructions or MT202 for bank-to-bank treasury cover. Remittance messages must identify the Canadian corporation by legal name, bank account number, SWIFT/BIC, and beneficiary account IBAN or Canadian transit number, and include a purpose narrative such as 'Unsolicited capital contribution / share subscription' or 'Related-party loan advance'. Canada does not maintain a mandatory purpose-code schedule, but FINTRAC reporting applies to electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Supporting documentation must include the share subscription agreement, board resolution, and a source-of-funds file demonstrating the economic legitimacy of the injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International supplier payments and operational disbursements should clear through SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlement, while documentary trade settlements use MT700/MT707 for commercial letters of credit under UCP600 and MT400/MT412 for documentary collections under URC522. Domestic CAD disbursements clear through Payments Canada Lynx using ISO 20022 messages; USD cross-border disbursements route through SWIFT with corresponding Fedwire or CHIPS settlement. Disbursement controls require dual signature authorization, an approved counterparty list, pre-transaction sanctions screening, and reconciliation of spot FX rates applied by the settlement bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla over-the-counter FX forwards with Canadian Schedule I banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to hedges involving illiquid or restricted currencies
FX call and put options transacted through IIROC-regulated dealers
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for matched long-term foreign-currency cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years triggers a notice of intent to dissolve; dissolution may follow after publication in the Canada Gazette; no administrative monetary penalty is automatically imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than the anniversary date of incorporation; if the anniversary falls on a non-business day, the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual declaration for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by the Registrar after a formal notice of intention to dissolve is issued.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based statutory audit threshold applies in Canada. All public or distributing corporations must annually appoint an independent auditor. A non-distributing private corporation may dispense with an audit by unanimous shareholder resolution, except where a court, Canada Revenue Agency, or a shareholder holding at least 5% of voting shares requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is acceptable for private corporations in Quebec and federally.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO confirmation filing exists in Quebec or federally. Federal CBCA corporations must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and update it within 15 days of knowledge of a change. Quebec QBCA corporations must maintain similar significant-control registers under provincial rules. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members; the annual return and annual declaration only confirm current directors, registered office, and corporate status.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (CBCA and QBCA)

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
